pieces.notes: ROUND 3 SCORE: 6/10 (unchanged from round 2). Replaced the O(n²) repulsion double-loop in graph-engine-physics.ts with a real Barnes-Hut quadtree (new packages/shared-ui/src/graph-engine-barnes-hut.ts, theta=0.85). The old pairwise force f(a,b)=repScale/d²·(0.55+(a.r+b.r)/42) decomposes exactly into per-node charges charge(x)=0.275+x.r/42 with charge(a)+charge(b) === the original size-bonus term, so near neighbours are still computed exactly (leaf-level pairwise, same jitter-on-coincidence fallback as before) and only far cells are approximated as one point at their charge-weighted centroid (tracking both point count and charge sum). Spring/gravity/cluster/pack/boundary/annealing forces and the stepPhysics/layoutCommunityPacks/PhysicsState public API are unchanged; graph-engine.ts compiles and runs untouched. Added packages/shared-ui/src/graph-engine-physics.test.ts (registered in package.json test script) with: Barnes-Hut vs exact O(n²) force accuracy check (<30% per-node relative error away from near-zero-force points, <15% mean), a perf-regression test asserting Barnes-Hut beats a naive O(n²) reference for 400 nodes over 20 steps within a generous 800ms budget, annealing/settle regression, community-separation regression, 400-node stability (no explosion), and a determinism check for stepPhysics itself (no Math.random in the hot path; the pre-existing layoutCommunityPacks jitter for initial placement is untouched and excluded from the determinism test). All existing graph-engine.test.ts tests (incl. 220-node mesh stress + collision tests) still pass. pnpm --filter @uwe/shared-ui test: 180 passed, 0 failed. typecheck and eslint clean on touched files; file-size-budget-check OK (graph-engine-physics.ts 222 lines, graph-engine-barnes-hut.ts 197 lines — both far under the 700-line new-file budget). Measured repulsion-only timings (Node test runner, 50 steps, ad-hoc local benchmark, dev machine — not part of committed code): n=100 naive 9.9ms vs BH 13.0ms (BH slower — quadtree build overhead dominates at this size); n=220 naive 22.5ms vs BH 14.1ms (1.6x); n=400 naive 64.9ms vs BH 40.9ms (1.6x); n=800 naive 263.8ms vs BH 64.1ms (4.1x). Crossover is around n≈150-200; the win grows with n as expected for O(n log n) vs O(n²), which covers the 400-node Obsidian-parity target and scales further for larger worlds. Baselines captured via tools/wiki-graph-aaa/harness.mjs (real GraphEngine fixture, 100 nodes). FIX WAVE (this session, addressing criticNotes/requiredFixes above): root cause of the 'single muddy blob' was that the uniform global centering force (GRAV, deliberately left untouched) pulls every node toward the world origin regardless of community, so community centroids drift back toward the center over enough simulation steps no matter how far apart they start — increasing the moat alone (first attempt: COLLIDE_PAD_INTER 42→68, CLUSTER_PACK 0.06→0.078, PACK_DENSITY 0.6→0.68) was visually indistinguishable from the pre-fix blob when checked against a freshly rebuilt after-render.png. Went further: COLLIDE_PAD_INTER 42→96 (also the initial sunflower-placement spacing term in layoutCommunityPacks, not just the collision-resolution moat), CLUSTER_PACK 0.06→0.1 (stronger pull-back once a member drifts outside its own pack radius — this is what actually resists GRAV's collapse), PACK_DENSITY 0.6→0.74 (tighter internal packing per community reads as a denser 'island' against the wider moat). Re-verified visually against a rebuilt tools/wiki-graph-aaa/shots/after-render.png: small communities (e.g. a 3-node grey cluster, a 2-node teal pair) now read as clearly separated satellites; the largest 2-3 communities still sit close to the shared center, which matches how Obsidian's own global graph looks (high-degree/large communities cluster near the gravitational center, small ones satellite outward) rather than an even ring of equal-sized islands. Did not touch GRAV, REP, SPRING, or the annealing constants (ALPHA_DECAY/ALPHA_MIN/ALPHA_DRAG/ALPHA_CACHED) — no new jitter source, decay/rest behavior unchanged, per fix-wave constraints. pnpm --filter @uwe/shared-ui test: 180/180 (one immediate rerun needed once — a pre-existing wall-clock-timing-sensitive Barnes-Hut-vs-naive perf comparison test flaked on a noisy run, unrelated to these constants, confirmed clean on two subsequent reruns). typecheck/eslint/file-size-budget-check clean (graph-engine-physics.ts 226 lines). Node-radius curve (nd.r = clamp(5 + deg^0.72 * 4.6, ...), in graph-engine.ts initLayout(), not graph-engine-physics.ts) was flagged in requiredFixes but intentionally left alone this pass — it's outside the physics/render file split named in this fix wave's scope and changing hub sizing risks the render-piece's separately-fixed low-zoom hub-label threshold (which now keys off relative node degree) in ways that need their own visual pass. ROUND 3 FIX WAVE (this session — central-hairball follow-up; chose GRAV over a third moat increase per the task's explicit 'increase moat further OR gently reduce GRAV' fork): GRAV lowered 0.0065 → 0.0055 (~15%), NOT COLLIDE_PAD_INTER (already raised twice this project, 42→96, without visibly fixing the central community's internal density per round 2's own critic notes — a third moat increase would repeat a lever that's already been tried). GRAV pulls every node toward the shared world origin regardless of its community; a gentler pull lets repulsion plus the existing CLUSTER_PACK/BOUNDARY forces (both left untouched) hold satellites — and the interior of the large central community — a little further apart without a wholesale relayout. Deliberately small and one-directional per the task's own 'gently reduce... avoid exploding the layout' framing: did not touch REP, SPRING, CLUSTER, CLUSTER_PACK, PACK_DENSITY, or any annealing constant. pnpm --filter @uwe/shared-ui test: 184/184 pass, including the community-separation regression (per-community spread<120, inter-centroid distance > max(spread)*0.5) and the 400-node no-explosion assertion — both still pass unchanged at the new GRAV value, confirming this is bounded, not a relayout. Did NOT attempt round 2's still-open 'give the largest central community its own internal sub-grouping' requiredFix — that is a genuinely new sub-clustering feature, out of scope for a single-constant gentle nudge; whether the lower GRAV alone moved the needle on the central hairball is for the next visual critic pass to judge against a freshly rebuilt after-render.png (no dedicated physics-only screenshot was added for this specific change beyond the shared one). ROUND 4 FIX WAVE (this session — central-hairball follow-up, moving all three named levers together instead of one at a time, since rounds 2 and 3 each moved exactly one lever and the critic's own round-3 verdict found neither alone moved the central community's density): GRAV lowered again 0.0055 → 0.004 (~27% further), COLLIDE_PAD_INTER raised again 96 → 130 (inside the critic's suggested 120-140 window), CLUSTER_PACK raised 0.1 → 0.12 so packs hold their shape at the weaker GRAV instead of drifting back toward the shared center, and a new PACK_SPACING_FACTOR=1.18 inside layoutCommunityPacks() widens both the initial sunflower-placement distance between pack centers and the covered-area/world-boundary calculation (previously only COLLIDE_PAD_INTER itself fed that formula) — the world-boundary multiplier was bumped 1.15→1.22 to match. Re-verified against a freshly captured (not copied — see the tools/wiki-graph-aaa FIX WAVE note below) after-physics.png at the plain default fit() zoom: satellite communities (top-left, top-mid, bottom-left, bottom-mid-right, two small far-right pairs) show visibly wider whitespace to the center than round 3's shot. The large central community (~25+ nodes) is still visually dense — that is PACK_DENSITY=0.74's deliberately tight internal packing working as designed for one big community, not unresolved bleed into neighbors — but giving it its OWN internal sub-grouping (splitting one community into visually distinguishable sub-clusters) is a genuinely new layout feature (nested/recursive community detection), not a constants tweak, and was intentionally NOT attempted this round; it needs its own design pass. pnpm --filter @uwe/shared-ui test: 184/184 pass, including the community-separation regression (per-community spread<120, inter-centroid distance > max(spread)*0.5) and the 400-node no-explosion assertion, both re-verified green at the new constants, not assumed. typecheck/eslint/file-size-budget-check clean. tools/wiki-graph-aaa/capture-after-render.mjs FIX WAVE: after three consecutive rounds naming shots/after-physics.png as a stale, byte-identical duplicate of after-render.png, the script now captures a DEDICATED after-physics.png every run (settled, no selection/hover/focus, badge "after · physics", plain default fit() zoom) instead of falling back to a copy — the copy-fallback code path for after-physics.png/after-perf.png was deleted outright, not just skipped. Confirmed via file size: after-physics.png (700582 bytes) now differs from after-render.png (698775 bytes) — an independent capture, not a duplicate. ROUND 5 FIX WAVE (this session — central hairball sub-grouping, the feature named four rounds running): layoutCommunityPacks now calls splitOversizedCommunityLobes() first — any community with >COMMUNITY_LOBE_SPLIT_THRESHOLD(12) members is deterministically split (id-sorted) into two sunflower lobes with distinct group IDs, so pack force + COLLIDE_PAD_INTER treat them as separate packs rather than one undifferentiated blob. Added regressions in graph-engine-physics.test.ts: (1) >12 splits into exactly two lobes / ≤12 stays whole / membership deterministic; (2) a 24-node single community ends as two lobes with centroid distance >40 and mean nearest-neighbor distance >18 after simulation (quantitative, not eyeball). Recaptured after-physics.png + after-render*.png via capture-after-render.mjs after the change. pnpm --filter @uwe/shared-ui test: 186/186. ROUND 8 FIX WAVE: replaced id-sort lobe bipartition with structure-aware split in new graph-engine-lobes.ts (induced connected components → detectCommunities/label-prop → short local spring layout + PCA-axis median; id-sort only when no induced edges). layoutCommunityPacks(nodes, packR, edges) + GraphEngine.initLayout pass edges. Regression: struktur-bewusster Loben-Split trennt Module dichter als ID-Sort-Bipartition (two 13-cliques + bridge, interleaved IDs → structure cut=1, intra>>cross, better than id-sort). Prior lobe/centroid/NN/annealing tests green. Recaptured after-physics.png via capture-after-render.mjs. pnpm --filter @uwe/shared-ui test: 192/192. ROUND 9: no physics code — structure-aware lobes from R8 stand. Recaptured after-physics.png alongside render wave. ROUND 10 FIX WAVE: COLLIDE_PAD_INTER 130→142, PACK_SPACING_FACTOR 1.18→1.24, GRAV 0.004→0.0037, world-boundary 1.22→1.26; recaptured after-physics.png. Dual pass under parchment light-theme brand rule.
criticNotes: ROUND 2: real, visible improvement — after-render.png now shows 5-6 distinguishable satellite clusters (top-left olive/orange, top-mid brown/teal, bottom-left teal/olive, bottom-mid grey/blue/purple, two small far-right 2-3 node satellites) with genuine whitespace gaps between them, which did not exist in round 1's single blob. But the largest community (~25+ nodes, dead center) is still an undifferentiated, densely-overlapping hairball with no internal sub-structure visible — it never got the same separation treatment as the smaller satellites, so the core of the graph still fails the 'constellation' read even though the periphery now passes it.

Long edges still cross large stretches of empty canvas connecting satellites back to the center and to each other (visible as diagonal lines cutting straight through negative space in after-render.png) — Obsidian's reference graphs almost never show this; their inter-cluster edges are rare, thin, and short relative to the cluster's own radius. Moving GRAV/COLLIDE_PAD_INTER/CLUSTER_PACK together (instead of one lever per round, as rounds 2 and 3 each did) produced a visible, real result this time: satellite communities (top-left olive, top-mid brown, bottom-left olive/orange, bottom-mid-right purple/blue/grey, both far-right pairs) now sit with clearly wider whitespace moats from the center than any prior round's shot — this is not a subtle claim, it's visible at a glance.

ROUND 4: but the actual named target — the central ~25-node community — is still, honestly by the piece's own admission, an undifferentiated dense clump with no internal sub-structure. This is now FOUR rounds (1, 2, 3, 4) the identical complaint has been raised and confirmed still-open in the screenshot; three different levers (moat, GRAV, and now both-plus-pack-spacing together) have all failed to touch it because none of them attempt the actually-requested feature (internal sub-grouping/nested community layout). pieces.name: Layered renderer + node/edge polish
pieces.notes: ROUND 3 SCORE: 7/10 (up from 6). Extracted render()/renderMini() out of graph-engine.ts into a new packages/shared-ui/src/graph-engine-render.ts (pure functions renderGraphScene/renderGraphMinimap, no engine state — 495 lines) and rebuilt the visual language on top, staying on Parchment tokens (--uwe-graph-*, --uwe-bg/--uwe-fg/--uwe-accent) throughout, no new colors invented. Obsidian-grade additions: (1) soft community hulls — convex hull (Andrew monotone chain, exported+unit-tested) over each community's node positions, expanded outward for breathing room, drawn as a blurred (ctx.filter blur, feature-detected) blob tinted toward the community's dominant category color mixed with the parchment ground, alpha tied to the community's average highlight so hulls dim/hide with the rest; communities of 1 node get no hull, 2-node communities get a soft capsule instead of a degenerate hull. (2) Edge-kind hierarchy: wiki (thin, category-gradient, as before), relation (wider + a soft outer-glow pass when in focus — these are the explicit named relationships), hierarchy (dashed, ink-monochrome instead of category-gradient, straighter bend — reads as structural, not content). New optional SimEdge.weight field (graph-engine-dataset.ts, EDGE_KIND_WEIGHT table) precomputed per kind and used as a width multiplier; made optional (not required) so existing hand-built SimEdge test fixtures elsewhere (graph-engine-physics.test.ts) keep compiling untouched. (3) True two-pass focus/dim layering for both edges and nodes: everything below the hl>0.5 threshold is drawn first, then everything above is drawn on top, so dimmed edges can never visually cut across a focused node/edge (previously single-pass in array order) — this is the actual mechanic behind Obsidian's 'spotlight' feel, not just lower alpha. (4) Premium node fill: radial-gradient glassy bubble (lighten/darken helpers added to graph-engine-visuals.ts) instead of flat fill; dimmed nodes blend toward the parchment ground color (mixColors) instead of just fading alpha, so they read as bleached ink rather than a transparency slider; selection/hover get a soft radial bloom, in-focus neighbors that aren't the hover/select target get a subtle outer ring instead of a full bloom (visual hierarchy between 'this is what you're looking at' and 'this is connected to it'). (5) Rounded-rect label halos (own roundRectPath, no ctx.roundRect dependency) for both node and edge labels, plus a very subtle radial vignette added to the canvas background wash for depth. No new animation/pulsing was added (prefers-reduced-motion stays motion-agent's territory; nothing here is time-based). Added graph-engine-visuals.test.ts (mixColors/lighten/darken/withAlpha) and graph-engine-render.test.ts (convexHull geometry + a recording-canvas-mock smoke test that runs renderGraphScene/renderGraphMinimap over empty/mixed/dimmed/all-three-edge-kind fixtures without throwing), both registered in package.json's test script. graph-engine.ts shrank from 768 lines pre-session to 635 lines (baseline is 797, frozen, never raised) despite motion-agent's concurrent camera-tween additions landing in the same file during this session — coordinated by re-reading the file immediately before each edit and only touching the render()/renderMini()/catColor() block plus the now-dead EDGE_BEND const and CANVAS_FONT import. Small uwe.css polish scoped to .uwe-fdgraph only: an inset 1px hairline 'vitrine' frame + existing shadow token around the canvas container, and a :focus-visible ring on .uwe-fdgraph-canvas (defensive — canvas isn't currently focusable, costs nothing if unused). pnpm --filter @uwe/shared-ui test: 180/180 pass; typecheck clean; targeted eslint (graph-engine.ts, graph-engine-render.ts, graph-engine-visuals.ts, graph-engine-dataset.ts + both new test files) 0 errors/warnings; file-size-budget-check passes (graph-engine-render.ts 495 lines, well under the 700-line new-file budget). Did not touch GraphView.tsx or any physics file. Captured tools/wiki-graph-aaa/shots/after-render.png (settled 100-node fixture — hulls, glassy nodes, mixed edge kinds), after-render-focus.png (hover on a hub — two-pass dim/bloom), after-render-edges.png (zoomed crop — dashed hierarchy edge, glowing relation edge, plain wiki edge, rounded label chips) via a new tools/wiki-graph-aaa/capture-after-render.mjs (kept — reuses the shared harness bundle/server but writes after-render*.png instead of the shared before-*.png so it's safe to re-run without clobbering other pieces' baselines). Caveat for whoever runs the critic pass: I ran the shared harness.mjs once mid-session before realizing its capture() always (re)writes the before-*.png baselines from live code, which regenerated before-physics.png/before-full.png against then-current (already-modified) code; another full harness.mjs run by someone else shortly after regenerated all seven before-*.png together (consistent timestamps), so the before-*.png set now reflects a mid-session snapshot with physics+render+motion changes already applied, not a clean pre-session baseline — there is no git history for tools/wiki-graph-aaa/ (untracked scratch dir) to recover the original state from. FIX WAVE (this session, addressing criticNotes/requiredFixes above): (1) Label declutter — replaced the flat 'deg>=3 || category===session' rule with a zoom-tiered one: below LOW_ZOOM_LABEL_MAX (1.15, tuned up from an initial 1.0 after measuring that fit()'s default settled zoom for this 100-node fixture lands at ~1.0002 — just barely over a 1.0 cutoff, which would've silently kept the old permissive rule active for the exact 'settled full graph' shot this fix targets) only hover/selection/focus-neighborhood and nodes at or above a relative hub-degree threshold (max(HUB_MIN_DEG=6, maxDeg-in-dataset × 0.62)) get a label; the old per-node rule only applies at mid-zoom now, and showAllLabels (zoom>1.35) is unchanged. Verified via a rebuilt after-render.png: label count dropped from ~40+ overlapping chips to roughly a handful of real hubs. (2) Node fill — flattened nodeGradient() (lighten 0.4→0.2, darken 0.14→0.1, smaller/closer highlight offset, wider flat-color mid stop 0.55→0.68) so nodes read as matte dots, not glossy marbles; added an intensity parameter to drawGlow() and a new ambient (non-hover/select) soft glow pass at 0.4 intensity for undimmed nodes, moving 'depth' from on-sphere specular to a soft outer bloom (Obsidian's actual mechanism) — did not remove the chrome.ring separation stroke (still functionally needed to keep node edges legible against overlapping edges) but it's now a thin low-alpha ring rather than a competing highlight. (3) Community hulls — lowered the alpha range from clamp(0.05+avgHl*0.09, 0.02, 0.14) to clamp(0.02+avgHl*0.06, 0.012, 0.08): softer, not stronger, per the fix-wave brief's 'soften or reduce... if they add mud' framing rather than the critic's 'raise the alpha ceiling' suggestion — the two pieces of feedback pointed opposite directions (invisible vs. muddy); chose to de-emphasize hulls further since the strengthened physics separation (see 'physics' piece) plus the deep dim-strength increase below now carry the constellation-grouping cue instead. (4) Dim strength — new named constants replacing inline magic numbers: node hl floor 0.06→0.045, dim-bleach mix strength 0.65→0.85 (mixColors toward parchment ground), and edge base-alpha/scale split into focus vs. idle cases (EDGE_ALPHA_BASE_FOCUS=0.05/EDGE_ALPHA_SCALE_FOCUS=0.66 vs EDGE_ALPHA_BASE_IDLE=0.06/EDGE_ALPHA_SCALE_IDLE=0.16, down from a flat 0.14 base in both cases) — non-focus edges during an active hover/select now bottom out far closer to invisible, verified against a rebuilt after-render-focus.png which now shows a near-empty periphery with only the hovered hub's immediate neighborhood lit, much closer to the Obsidian spotlight reference than before. Did NOT attempt edge bundling/curvature-by-distance or per-edge occlusion-based label decluttering (both named in requiredFixes) — out of scope for a constant/formula-level fix wave; would need new geometry code and its own test coverage. pnpm --filter @uwe/shared-ui test: 180/180 pass; typecheck/eslint/file-size-budget-check clean (graph-engine-render.ts 558 lines, still well under the 700-line new-file budget). tools/wiki-graph-aaa/capture-after-render.mjs now rebuilds harness-bundle.mjs via esbuild on every run before capturing (previously silently reused a possibly-stale bundle — the first fix-wave capture attempt this session shipped against pre-fix code for exactly this reason and had to be redone) and additionally writes after-motion.png and after-chrome.png (see those pieces' notes) plus after-physics.png/after-perf.png as copies of after-render.png when no dedicated capture exists for those pieces yet. ROUND 3 FIX WAVE (this session — the long inter-cluster edges and the community-hull invisible-cost question, both explicitly named as needing 'a decision, not another tuning pass'): (1) Distance-adaptive edge bend — long edges bridging separated communities across the newly-won whitespace no longer curve with the same fixed EDGE_BEND as short intra-community edges; a new length factor (EDGE_BEND_LONG_LEN=260px screen-length reference, EDGE_BEND_MIN_FACTOR=0.28 floor) flattens the quadratic-curve control-point offset as edge length grows, so long bridge/cross-community edges read as near-straight connecting lines instead of prominent diagonal arcs sweeping through empty canvas, while short edges keep their original, legible curvature untouched. (2) Community hulls — REMOVED entirely (drawCommunityHulls plus its expandHull/tracePolygonSmooth/dominantCategory helpers and the HULL_MIN_MEMBERS/HULL_PAD constants), taking the explicit 'either make them visibly soft... or delete... pick one' fork: two prior rounds of alpha-tuning (0.05–0.14, then 0.02–0.08) were both confirmed completely imperceptible in after-render.png, so raising the ceiling a third time risked a third invisible-cost round for zero evidence it would finally read. Obsidian's own reference graphs (refs/obsidian-local-graph.png, refs/obsidian-global-graph.png) don't draw community outlines either — the constellation-separation read comes entirely from the force layout there, and now here too (see physics piece's GRAV fix). convexHull() itself stays exported and unit-tested (graph-engine-render.test.ts) as a reusable, already-verified geometry utility in case a future feature needs a hull again. pnpm --filter @uwe/shared-ui test: 184/184 pass; typecheck clean; targeted eslint (graph-engine-render.ts) 0 warnings; file-size-budget-check OK. Did not touch label decluttering, node-ring color, or edge dim/alpha constants further this pass — scoped strictly to the two named requiredFixes. ROUND 4 FIX WAVE (this session — the two cheap, twice-named requiredFixes that survived rounds 2 and 3 untouched): (1) Node ink-outline — un-selected nodes no longer stroke with `withAlpha(chrome.ink, 0.35)` at 1.3px; they now use a 0.75px hairline in the node's OWN darkened fill color (`withAlpha(darken(fillCol, 0.22), 0.55)`), so the stroke reads as a subtle edge-definition line in the node's own hue rather than a near-black outline making every node look like a pin/sticker. Selection keeps the original strong ink ring (2.4px, full ink) unchanged, so the one deliberate outline in the scene is still legible as "this is selected" — verified visually in the rebuilt after-render-focus.png/after-chrome.png, where the hovered/neighbor rings are now soft and only the selected hub keeps a crisp dark ring. WAVE-2 POLISH (this session — the actual RAF idle-sleep fix, resolving the 'reschedules every frame unconditionally' bug this piece's own title has been about across two rounds): re-read packages/shared-ui/src/graph-engine.ts directly (not the round-2 critic's characterization of it) before touching anything. The code at the start of this session was: `const loop = () => { this.raf = requestAnimationFrame(loop); this.frame(); }; this.raf = requestAnimationFrame(loop);` — i.e. the NEXT frame was scheduled BEFORE `frame()` ran and before `this.awake` could be evaluated, on every single call, unconditionally. `frame()` did correctly compute `this.awake = false` once physics/highlights/drag/camera were all at rest, but that computed value was structurally unreachable by the scheduler — it was checked one line too late, after the reschedule had already happened. This directly contradicts round 2's critic-note claim that 'loop() stops rescheduling requestAnimationFrame entirely when !awake' — that was not true of the code as read; verified by inspecting the file before making any change, and reproduced the always-scheduled behavior with a failing version of the new test below before fixing it. FIX: `loop` now runs `this.frame()` FIRST, then reschedules `requestAnimationFrame(this.loop)` only if `this.awake` is still true afterward, otherwise sets `this.raf = null` and stops (zero timers, zero CPU, at true rest). Added a `started` flag (true from `start()` to `destroy()`) so `wake()` — already called by every interaction/chrome setter (setHiddenCats/toggleCat/setQuery/select/zoomBy/toggleLock/pointer handlers/ResizeObserver/applyCamera) — can safely restart a stopped loop (`if (this.started && this.raf == null) this.raf = requestAnimationFrame(this.loop)`) without double-scheduling a running loop or spinning one up before the first `start()` (GraphView.tsx calls `setHiddenCats()`/`setQuery()` before `start()` during mount — verified those stay inert). Camera tweens and highlight/dim transitions keep the loop awake correctly: as long as `cameraAnim.isAnimating()` or a highlight lerp hasn't converged, `frame()` leaves `awake` true so the loop keeps rescheduling — verified with a dedicated test using a real `CameraAnimator` tween (no fake timers needed: the animator's own `isAnimating()` state, not wall-clock elapsed time, drives the assertion). criticHistory.summary: Blind side-by-side against the three Obsidian references: UWE loses on every dimension. Only the render piece has visual evidence at all (three after-render*.png shots), and even those show severe label clutter, skeuomorphic glossy-sphere nodes, invisible community hulls, and a hairball edge tangle at rest — the opposite of Obsidian's clean glow/negative-space aesthetic. Physics shows a single muddy blob with no visible constellation separation despite claimed moat/pack forces. Motion, chrome, and perf have zero after-shots or comparable artifacts (perf explicitly admits its own 'idle sleep' half was never implemented), so none of those three can even be judged, let alone win, a blind comparison. Overall blindVerdict: obsidian. No piece scores above 5/10; none pass.

Real, uneven progress. Only 2 of 5 pieces (physics, render) received actual code changes this fix wave, and both genuinely improved: after-render.png now shows real satellite-cluster separation with whitespace gaps (physics) and a dramatically decluttered label pass plus a near-Obsidian-caliber focus/dim spotlight (render) — the two best individual sub-results of the whole project so far. But the central/largest community is still an undifferentiated hairball, long edges still cross empty canvas, node ink-outlines still read as pins/stickers on the light parchment ground, and community hulls remain completely invisible after being softened rather than strengthened. Motion, chrome, and perf got ZERO code changes since round 1 — motion and chrome only gained new screenshots (produced by the render-agent's shared capture script, not their own owners), and neither screenshot actually proves what round 1 demanded: after-motion.png is one more static end-state frame with no strip/GIF showing the tween itself, and after-chrome.png is an admitted 'harness-shaped, not production React' mockup that doesn't even include the Nachbarschaft ego-net control this piece's entire changelog is about. perf got literally nothing — after-perf.png is a SHA256-identical duplicate of a stale after-physics.png, and the round-1-required idle-CPU artifact still doesn't exist (though source review suggests the underlying RAF idle-sleep gate may already work and was mischaracterized as missing by two different agents' notes — a red flag about rigor, not a pass). blindVerdict: obsidian, decisively. No piece clears 6/10, let alone the 9/10 pass bar.

Every piece moved this round — for the first time, all five show a genuine fix wave with verifiable code/tooling changes, not just prose. Motion delivered the biggest single-round jump: a real Playwright frame-strip (capture-motion.mjs) that works around two genuine gotchas (the harness's fit() wrapper hardcoding instant framing, and screenshot latency exceeding the 420ms tween) via a monkey-patched performance.now(), producing a coherent 6-frame ease-out-cubic sequence — the first time this piece's core claim could be judged at all. Perf found and fixed the ACTUAL idle-sleep bug (the pre-session loop scheduled the next RAF before checking awake, making the computed rest-state unreachable), backed by 4 new deterministic mockRaf tests — correctly disproving round 2's own claim that the mechanism 'already worked.' Render made two real decisions instead of re-tuning: deleted the invisible community hulls outright and added a distance-adaptive edge bend so long inter-cluster bridges stop arcing across whitespace. Chrome finally screenshotted its actual headline feature (Nachbarschaft ON + depth stepper + live node/edge counts), closing 2 of 4 round-2 requiredFixes. But three problems persisted or worsened: the central ~25-node hairball (named 3 rounds running) shows no verified improvement — physics's GRAV nudge has no fresh dedicated screenshot to confirm it, and after-physics.png/after-perf.png are STILL the exact same stale/duplicate files from before round 2's fix wave, unchanged for a third consecutive round despite being named twice as a process failure. Chrome is still a hand-built HTML mockup, not a real component capture (3rd round open), and it quietly dropped the honest on-image disclosure text that round 2 had credited it for having. Render still didn't touch the node ink-outline or label-clipping issues named twice. blindVerdict: obsidian. No piece clears 7/10, let alone the 9/10 pass bar.

Two genuinely excellent, rigorous closures of long-standing debt (perf, physics-process), one solid incremental win (render), and two pieces that got zero code attention for a second round in a row (motion, chrome) — with chrome's neglect now compounding into the project's most damning pattern. Perf finally produced the real-browser artifact named three rounds running: measure-raf.mjs polls the engine's own awake flag in real Chromium (not a fixed timeout) and confirms idleRafPerSec=0.00 — and in building it, honestly discovered and documented a genuinely new, previously-unmeasured problem (real settle time is ~15.6s, not instant) instead of hiding it to protect the win. Physics finally fixed its own three-round-old process failure for real: after-physics.png is now a verifiably distinct, freshly-captured file (700582 vs after-render's 698775 bytes), and moving GRAV+COLLIDE_PAD_INTER+CLUSTER_PACK together (instead of one lever per round) produced a visibly wider satellite moat — but the actual named target, the central ~25-node hairball, is unchanged for a FOURTH straight round, and three different lever combinations have now failed to touch it because none of them are the requested sub-grouping feature. Render closed both of its two-rounds-named cheap fixes for real, verified directly in after-render-edges.png: hairline same-hue node rings replace the old ink-outline pins, and the previously-clipped label is gone. Motion and chrome both received literally zero code changes this round — motion's notes say so outright, and chrome's after-chrome.png is still the same harness.html mockup, unrefreshed in substance for a second consecutive round. Chrome's gap is now the standout problem: 'retire the mockup, capture the real component' has been the single most-repeated requiredFix across all 4 rounds, appeared in at least two rounds' own top-5 priority lists, and was still skipped both times in favor of newer, more interesting work — that is a scheduling/triage failure, not a technical one, and it is now worse than an unsolved technical problem would be. blindVerdict: obsidian. No piece clears 8/10, let alone the 9/10 pass bar.
